title: Your categories survive the bank changing its mind
body: Banks quietly reformat transaction descriptions — a Zelle payment gets masked, fields get shuffled — and when that happened, a category you'd taught the app could silently stop applying. One month your rent is there, the next it's gone from the picture entirely, and nothing told you. Now the app matches on the part that never changes — the actual merchant words — with the throwaway reference codes stripped out. Every category you've already taught keeps working exactly as before; this only catches the ones a format change would have dropped. One more brick in making the numbers trustworthy enough to run your life on.

title: Categorize your money right from your phone
body: The web app can finally do the money-sorting work itself. If you use the Cache in a browser (or on your phone's home screen), the categorize tools used to say 'no data — sync first' even with your bank connected, and every tag was desktop-only. Now the merchant and deposit lists come straight from your own encrypted cache, and tagging works right there: assign categories in Money Map, define what counts as income in What makes money, and watch the numbers recompute on the spot. Your tags seal into your encrypted vault and sync to every device — and if you tag the same thing on two devices, the newest edit wins cleanly.

title: Your burn rate tells the truth now
body: Moving money between your own accounts — and paying your credit card — is not spending, and the app now agrees everywhere. Before this, the board's headline numbers (burn per day, spending total, the trend, Safe to spend) quietly counted your own transfers as money spent, which could inflate them badly if you move money around a lot. And hand-categorizing a transaction as a transfer removed it from the category list but left the totals stale until your next bank sync. One rule now, on every path and every device: money leaving your life counts, money moving between your own pockets never does — with the excluded amount shown honestly as a footnote in Where it's going.

title: Your bug reports, squashed — bucket on phones, saner sessions, chimes that chime
body: A whole pass driven by beta reports (thank you — every one earned its keep). Brain Bucket now works on your phone: it used to live only on the desktop server, so the web app couldn't store a thought — now it lives in your synced, encrypted cache on every device, and your existing items migrate in on their own. Sessions grew up: the screen stops jumping to the top on every tap, it says which day you're logging, and stats + minutes belong to the day you tapped on the calendar — so the calendar row and the open session finally tell the same story. Ending or skipping a work block early now banks the minutes you actually put in. The work/rest chime rings on iPhones again (iOS quietly mutes audio when an app backgrounds; we now wake it first). Friend requests you've already seen stop lighting up the message badge. And tapping a text box on your phone no longer zooms the whole page.

title: Colour-coded calendar, softer board, clearer names
body: A few looks-and-feel passes. Your calendar now colour-codes every item by kind and labels it — event, session, task, routine, habit — so a glance tells you what's what, in month, week, and day views. Widgets on your board are now pressed gently into the surface (a soft, tactile, embossed feel) instead of floating as glass cards — and it re-tones itself to every theme. And the Note widget is now called Post-it note, so it's no longer confused with the notes inside your deck.

title: Sessions — schedule focused time and track it your way
body: Schedule a session on your calendar — a practice block, a deep-work stretch — and tap it to open a focused space with three flexible ways to track it, use any or all: the work/rest timer right there (point it at the session and finished blocks bank minutes toward a goal, filling a progress bar), a task checklist, and custom stats you define — a number like hours practiced or panels completed, a yes/no, a 1–5 rating, or a few words. It's built for the goals that are about showing up and putting in the time — an instrument, a craft, an art practice — where the win is the hours, not a checklist. Everything syncs across your devices; the running timer stays on the device you're using.

title: Projects — group the work and watch it move
body: A new Projects widget, for the bigger efforts that don't fit in a flat to-do list. Add it from the Widget Library, name a project, open it, and add the tasks it takes — check them off and the project's progress bar fills up. A project's tasks live inside the project instead of scattering through your loose Tasks list, and everything syncs task by task across your devices. This is v1 — progress is a simple task count for now; due dates, habits inside a project, and projects that span more than one area of your life are on the way.

title: Build your routine right where you edit it
body: Open a routine and you can now shape it in place: add a step, rename it, reorder it with the arrows, or remove one — no more bouncing back to the deck card to hunt for the little ＋. Each step is a real task that rides with the routine everywhere it shows, and everything you change syncs to your other devices on its own.

title: One calm dot for all your connections
body: The big green SYNCED button is gone. Tap the little cloud dot at the bottom of the board and you get one quiet panel that shows, in plain words, whether your three lifelines are healthy: cloud sync, your bank, and (on the desktop) the local cache server. Each has a colour-and-shape light so it reads at a glance even in the black-and-white theme or if you're colour-blind — a green dot means good, an open ring or square means it wants you. Sync now lives right there, and so do your account controls (cloud settings, switch account, log out). Less clutter on the board, and when something needs you, it's obvious where to look.

title: Your recovery file now lands in the browser too
body: The safety net that hands you a recovery file used to only kick in on the desktop app — so if you live in the web app, you never got one. Now you do: the first time you open your cache in the browser, if you don't already have a recovery file, your cache makes one and offers it to you with a single tap. Keep it somewhere safe and a forgotten passphrase can never lock you out. It stays zero-knowledge the whole time — we still can't read your data — and it only ever appears once, never nagging you on later logins.

title: Old accounts get a recovery net — automatically
body: If you've had a cache since before recovery files existed, your vault used to have no safety net: forget your passphrase and it was gone for good. Not anymore. The next time you open your cache with your passphrase, we quietly upgrade it and hand you a recovery file to keep somewhere safe — so a forgotten passphrase can never lock you out again. It stays zero-knowledge the whole time (we still can't read your data), your passphrase keeps working exactly as before, and if anything goes wrong the upgrade simply doesn't happen — your cache is never left half-changed.

title: Verify your email — a gentle checkbox, never a gate
body: Confirming your email address is now a Cache Health item you can check off — it makes sure a password reset or recovery can actually reach you. It never blocks you from signing in or using your cache; it's just one more thing your cache nudges you to finish. A verification email goes out when you make an account (resend any time from Settings → Cache cloud), and the moment you click the link, it checks itself off.

title: Forgot your password? Reset it yourself
body: A quiet "Forgot password?" link now sits under the sign-in fields — on the web and in Settings → Cache cloud. Confirm your email and we send a reset link. It always says the same calm thing whether or not that email has an account, so it can't be used to find out who's registered. And it's honest about what a reset does: getting back into your account isn't the same as unlocking your data. If your cache is sealed just for you (zero-knowledge), the link gets you in, but your data still opens only with your recovery file or code — so the app says exactly that and points you there, instead of pretending your data is back. Accounts that keep a spare key with us just open as normal. The reset and email-verification links now land on The Cache's own clean page — set your new password right there — instead of a bare hosting page.

title: Your cache is yours — zero-knowledge by default
body: New accounts are now sealed so only you can open them — we can't read your data, by math, not policy. So you can't get locked out, every account gets a recovery file to save at setup (add a recovery code too if you like), and any one of them opens your cache. Prefer we keep a spare key to help you back in? That's now a clear opt-in checkbox, off by default. Manage all your unlock methods any time in Settings → Cache cloud. Existing accounts keep working exactly as before.

title: Connect your bank right from your phone
body: No computer needed. Paste your SimpleFIN setup token on the web and your cache pulls your balances and transactions itself, then syncs them to your other devices — all computed on your device, sealed so the cloud can't read it. SimpleFIN holds the bank login (we never see it) and the key stays on your phone (so we can't see your money either). Tap the new "How does this work?" for a plain walkthrough. Sync when you want; it always tells you how fresh your numbers are.

title: What changed finds you now
body: When something new ships, your cache tells you — a short "What's changed" note opens when you sign in, or right when an update lands if you're already here. It waits if you're mid-sentence, never shows the same thing twice, and everything is still in the bell whenever you want it.

title: A calmer dock, and a tidier profile
body: The cloud button moved into the dock and stopped resizing itself every time it synced — no more dock sliding around under your cursor. Your profile folds its activity into one line you can open in its own window, and account switching works from there. The Roadmap button is now an option you can turn on rather than a default.

title: Get your money in — right in the browser
body: The web app can now take money in on its own, no desktop required. Download a CSV from your bank and drop it onto your cache (or Menu → Import statement) — your browser builds your ledger and works out your spending, safe-to-spend and income, then syncs it to your devices, sealed so the cloud never sees it. Re-import as often as you like; duplicates are skipped.

title: News lands here now
body: Messages grew a second inbox: What's new. Every update we ship shows up here — quietly. A small mark on the bottom corner of the messages button means there's news; the top corner is still people. Nothing here ever interrupts you.
